question.problem:
Solve the following congruence:

$$
5x+4≡23\,(\text{mod}\,13)
$$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce our congruence to a congruence of the form $ax≡b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+4 & ≡23\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 5x+4-4 & ≡23-4\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 5x & ≡19\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 5x & ≡1\cdot 13+6\, & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 5x & ≡6\, & (\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=5$ and $n=13$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(5,13)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,13).$ To find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,13)$, we compute the exponents of $5\,(\text{mod}\,13)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,13):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25≡1\cdot 13+12≡12 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡12\cdot 5≡60≡4\cdot 13+8≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ {5}^{4} & ≡8\cdot 5≡40≡3\cdot 13+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $8\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,13),$ which means that $8$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $13$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $8,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 8\cdot 5x & ≡8\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ (8\cdot 5)x & ≡48 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡9+3\cdot 13 &  & (\text{mod}\,13) \\ x & ≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,13)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡9\,(\text{mod}\,13).$
